This is more likely to cause downstream clarification/extra work than direct harm in this case.

Omitting a denial of nausea has minimal impact in an acute wheeze/asthma-type presentation, as it is not a key discriminator or safety-critical red flag here. It primarily reduces completeness of documentation.

Omitting a denial of vomiting is unlikely to change assessment or management for isolated wheeze/shortness of breath in this context. The main effect is reduced ROS completeness rather than clinical decision error.
